process_observations.observation: The loop caught a defect no checker in this build could have caught. check_case_management_setup.py exits 0 on both the as-built file and the rebuilt one; the three missing elements were only ever visible to the org's own validation. That is the mock-deploy stage doing precisely the job it exists for, one milestone before the gate.

Three facts that decide whether this file deploys are absent from both cited skills: systemUserEmail entirely (zero hits across either skill package), newEntityRecordType's value shape, and newEntityRecordType's API 64.0 floor. The as-built run behaved correctly by its own contract - Step 5 rule 1 forbade guessing - and still produced a file the org refuses. A rule that prevents fabrication does not, on its own, prevent an undeployable artefact when the library is thin.

F-27 silently invalidates a design decision recorded in two places. M4-S03's before-save flow is specified to stamp Priority 'guarded so it writes only into a null value', and the as-built M3-S03 deliberately left casePriority blank so that guard would fire. The org's requirement removes that option for the email channel only, so the two intake channels now diverge: email arrives at Medium, web arrives blank. Recorded in both notes rather than left for M4-S03 to discover.

casePriority Medium is a skill default, not an answer. No clarification among the 97 says which CasePriority value either channel should stamp, and no CasePriority standard value set exists under artefacts/ to validate it against - the org accepting it proves the value exists in THAT org's picklist and nothing more. Whether Medium is right for a billing channel with its own SLA ladder is unadjudicated.

systemUserEmail's value is unprovisioned. support-noreply@acme.example was chosen (by the operator) to be visibly not either inbound routing address, which is the right shape for avoiding both an inbound loop and a mistaken reading as the acknowledgement sender - but no step in this build creates or verifies that mailbox, and the guide does not say whether the platform sends to it, from it, or merely records it.

The rebuild is minimal and auditable: three added elements and one version string. Diffing the before/after hashes of all five artefacts shows web-to-case-form-contract.md untouched, and the two XML files differ only by the four operator-proven changes.
